questions.q: An ordinary node gets a batch of 4 images on one wire. How many times is it called?
questions.why: A batch is one item in the list the engine carries.

questions.q: An ordinary node gets a list of 4 images on one wire and a number widget. How many calls?
options: Four, and the widget is lost
An error, as the lengths differ
questions.why: One call per item of the longest list. A shorter list repeats its last item.

questions.q: Lists of 3 and 2 meet at a node. What is the third call?
options: Third of a, first of b
Third of a, second of b
questions.answer: Third of a, second of b
questions.why: The shorter list repeats its last item. The lab prints (3, 20).

questions.q: You set INPUT_IS_LIST. How does an INT widget with value 5 arrive?
questions.why: The flag covers every input. Our real run saw k=[1], and core reads final_width[0].

questions.q: Your function returns a list, and you did not set OUTPUT_IS_LIST. What does the next node get?
options: One call, with the whole list as a single value
questions.answer: One call, with the whole list as a single value
questions.why: Without the flag, merge_result_data keeps your list as one item.
